headline: CLIENT MONDAY, AND THE CLOCK ON THE BOARD IS THE 198 RENA LISTING AGREEMENT, WHICH FOUR SEPARATE SOURCES READ AS EXPIRING TODAY — meanwhile the weekend's loudest alarm turned out to be false: the automation platform is ALIVE, verified on the live instrument this morning, and the three routines that called it dead were all quoting the same vendor email. · DO: call Ann & Don C. — 198 Rena expires today · WATCH: automatic drafts still exceed the cash they draw from, day 15 unposted.

notes: 🟢 THE BIGGEST FLEET NEWS THIS MORNING IS A CORRECTION, NOT A FAILURE — THE AUTOMATION PLATFORM IS NOT DOWN. Three separate routines went to bed Saturday night reporting it dead, one of them forecasting a thirteen-day blackout. This morning's live check of the platform itself says every scenario is running, the organization is not paused, and one job is already scheduled for later today. Three independent receipts back it: the instant-lead alert fired at 2:37 this morning, seven hours after the supposed outage; you yourself logged into the platform twenty-nine minutes after the alarm went out; and this morning's letter was delivered through the very send path that was declared dark. ⭐ WHY IT MATTERED ENOUGH TO BECOME A RULE: all three alarms traced to ONE vendor email quoted three times, which is exactly why the two-source check did not catch it. A new hard rule shipped this morning — never report the platform's state from an email, read the live instrument — and it explicitly disqualifies the one field the routines had been trusting. ⚠️ The cause of the recovery is deliberately NOT asserted: the licence carries a grace period, so running today does not prove the meter refilled. Billing stays a you-decision.

✅ THE MONDAY MORNING WAVE LANDED CLEAN AND ON TIME, WHICH IS NOT A GIVEN — this is the first Monday in three weeks with every anchor present. The money report, the finance pulse, the trading cockpit, the inbox triage, the weekly forecast, the marketing engine and the morning letter all ran between 5:30 and 7:00 and all wrote fresh handoffs. ⭐ The lead lane opened exactly at seven as the rule requires and immediately released the weekend queue: three first touches went out inside thirteen minutes to sellers who had raised their hands on Sunday, and a fourth brand-new buyer was answered six minutes after he arrived at 7:00. Nothing was sent early, and nothing that was owed was missed.

⚠️ TWO REAL DEFECTS, NEITHER FATAL, BOTH NAMED RATHER THAN ABSORBED. The bookkeeping routine hit a sign-in wall on the accounting platform for the THIRD consecutive run — the reading connection still works, but nothing can be posted, and the half-year books have now come back byte-identical three times running, which means two weeks of zero progress against a filing deadline four weeks out. ⚠️ Separately, the team board ran PARTIAL: the usual way of confirming lead ownership returned essentially no real people, because a two-thousand-row bulk import under another agent's name is still filling the whole visible window. It fell back to a per-record check and the board went out correctly, but the shortcut is still blocked. 🛑 And one item is fully self-inflicted and worth saying plainly: this fleet now has TWO drafts sitting on the same negotiation thread, the second written by the machine at 5:55 this morning. It flagged its own duplicate rather than letting you find it.

callBlock.who: Amy G. of Ethos International — her buyers put 355 Comanche TOP OF THEIR LIST, and this is day three
callBlock.why: 🔥 STILL THE HOTTEST THING ON THE BOARD, AND IT HAS NOW SURVIVED A FULL WEEKEND UNWORKED. She filed Saturday at 11:24 PM off that afternoon's tour: interested — YES, and in her own words her buyers have just started looking, really like the property, and have put it at the top of their list. ⭐ WHAT MAKES THIS DIFFERENT FROM EVERY OTHER YES ON THIS HOUSE: she is the same agent who phoned you from inside the home mid-showing, and you already answered half of what she asked by text. This is a returned call, not a cold approach. 🔴 THE HALF YOU DID NOT ANSWER IS STILL OPEN — she reported the basement lights would not come on, and buyers who have 'just started looking' will tour more houses this week with a dark basement as their last memory of yours. ⚠️ SAID HONESTLY RATHER THAN ASSUMED: this is the second consecutive morning with no receipt that the call happened. A call from the truck leaves no trace, so this is reported as no evidence, NOT as 'you didn't call' — but a third pass with nothing is where it gets escalated. ⭐ She left BOTH price fields blank and scored staging a 3 — the only agent to score staging since the cut, so ask her what she would change.

callBlock.who: James P. — a $1.89M Indian Springs owner who says YOUR estimate on his own house is TOO LOW
callBlock.why: 🔥 THE HIGHEST-INTENT SHAPE A SELLER LEAD EVER TAKES, AND IT IS THE BIGGEST NUMBER TO ARRIVE IN WEEKS. He came to your site on Sunday morning, saw the automated value on his Miller Circle property, and told you it was too low. ⭐ AN OWNER ARGUING ABOUT HIS OWN NUMBER IS NOT BROWSING — he has a price in his head, which means he has a plan, and he is inviting the conversation about what the house is really worth. ✅ OWNERSHIP IS FULLY SETTLED ON THIS ONE: it cleared BOTH verification methods this morning and the shared-pool question was affirmatively ruled out, so the caveat that sat on this record over the weekend is dead. ✅ His first touch went out at 7:13 this morning, the moment the send window opened — so the call is now the follow-through, not the opener. ⏰ Sunday hand-raise, Monday call. That is the whole window.

callBlock.who: Christopher L. — second homeowner in one weekend to call your estimate on his own house TOO LOW
callBlock.why: 🔥 THE SAME SHAPE AS THE ONE ABOVE, ON THE SAME WEEKEND, WHICH IS THE PATTERN WORTH NOTICING. He told your site that the estimate on his Lake Circle home was too low. Two owners disputing their own valuations upward inside twenty-four hours is not a coincidence — it is what a market with rising seller confidence looks like from inside your own data. ⭐ THE ANSWER IS NOT A NUMBER, IT IS A CONVERSATION: he is telling you he thinks his house is worth more, and the fastest way to a listing appointment is to agree that the automated estimate is a starting point and offer to do the real one by hand. ✅ First touch went out this morning inside the window. ⏰ Both of these decay fast — a seller who raises a hand on Sunday is talking to somebody by Wednesday.

callBlock.who: Thomas D. — he said YES, he has the document he asked for, and nobody has called
callBlock.why: ✅ THIS IS THE ONE THAT UNBLOCKED ITSELF AND THEN STALLED ANYWAY. He replied 'Yes' on Friday and asked for the 19-lot layout and the per-acre number. 🆕 THE PLAT WAS LOCATED AND EMAILED THE SAME MORNING — the exact deliverable his open chip had been waiting on. ⭐ SO THE CALL IS NO LONGER A HOLDING REPLY, IT IS A FOLLOW-UP ON SOMETHING HE ALREADY HAS IN HAND, which is a completely different conversation. 🔥 He is one of eight names off the 19-lot land ad, and that ad remains the only advertising in the portfolio producing anything at all — two more names came off it over the weekend, including one who registered on your own site four minutes later. ⏰ Two days since he answered. The gap between 'he said yes' and 'nobody called' is where this one dies.

callBlock.who: Cassie C. of RE/MAX Advantage — she wrote the offer, called the old price too high, and still has not been told it moved
callBlock.why: 🔴 NINE DAYS OVERDUE, AND THE WEEKEND MADE THE CASE STRONGER RATHER THAN WEAKER. Her buyer toured 355 Comanche in late July, she wrote the offer, and she called the ask too high — at a number that no longer exists. She has never been told the price came down. ⭐ FIVE CONSECUTIVE READS SINCE THE CUT HAVE NOW DECLINED TO ARGUE THE NUMBER, including Saturday night's YES. The pricing question on this house is settled; what is not settled is that an agent who already wrote one offer is still working off a dead figure. ⛔ Quote the current list price only, and CALL rather than email — co-op agents sit in the no-email lane under your own rule, and that rule is exactly what the fleet is still waiting on you to revisit, now ten days.

callBlock.who: Angela B. of Keller Williams Vestavia — interested buyer, same dead price, same nine days
callBlock.why: 🔴 THE TWIN OF THE ROW ABOVE AND IT COSTS THE SAME THING. Her buyer toured 355 Comanche in early August, she filed interested — YES, and she called the ask too high. Like Cassie, she filed before the cut and has never heard the number moved. ⭐ TWO AGENTS WITH INTERESTED BUYERS ON YOUR HIGHEST-TRAFFIC ACTIVE LISTING, BOTH WORKING OFF A PRICE THAT NO LONGER EXISTS, is the cheapest fixable loss on the whole board — it costs two phone calls and no negotiation. ⛔ Same rule: current list price only, and call rather than email.

callBlock.who: Gloria F. — the tenant answer is now twenty-four days owed
callBlock.why: 🔴 THE LONGEST-RUNNING BROKEN PROMISE ON THE BOARD, AND IT CROSSED THREE WEEKS THIS WEEKEND. She waited nineteen days without complaining, then escalated three times in twenty-seven minutes on a Wednesday night — two voicemails and a text. ✅ THE EMERGENCY HALF RESOLVED WITHOUT YOU: power is back on at the property and the tenant paid his balance, both confirmed. ⭐ THAT MAKES THE CALL EASIER, NOT UNNECESSARY — what she actually asked is still unanswered: is the tenant out, because he owes another month if he is not. ⭐ YOU DO NOT NEED THE ANSWER TO MAKE THE CALL, and waiting for one is precisely what turned six days into twenty-four. ⭐ Monday is Client Day, and she is not a loose end — she closed with you in June and still opens your market reports.

callBlock.who: Will S. — off the 19-lot land ad, then onto your own site four minutes later
callBlock.why: 🆕 THE STRONGEST SIGNAL SHAPE A NEW LEAD PRODUCES, BECAUSE IT IS TWO CHANNELS IN FOUR MINUTES. He clicked the 19-lot ad on Sunday afternoon and then registered on your IDX site four minutes behind it — that combination is materially stronger evidence of real intent than either action on its own, because he went looking for more after the ad did its job. ✅ First touch went out this morning at 7:10, held to the window rather than fired on a Sunday. ⭐ He is the third-plus name off this one ad, on a package listing where the ad is doing all the work the rest of the portfolio is not. ⏰ Roughly fifteen hours old — still inside the window where speed matters.

listings.status: ⏰ Active $450K — the listing agreement expires TODAY and the decision is still unruled
listings.note: ⏰ THIS IS THE CLOCK ON THE BOARD. Four independent sources now read 08-17 — the CRM crawl, your operations manager's board reminder due today, the chip that first caught the conflict, and this morning's marketing brief — so the agreement runs out TODAY, not last Friday. This board printed 8/14 twice and was wrong both times; the correction is logged rather than quietly swapped. ⚠️ AND IT IS A REINSTATEMENT, NOT AN EXTENSION — that came from Don himself Saturday morning, along with the fact that Mrs Ann had not yet been asked. 🔴 NO LANE HAS EVER SIGHTED THE ACTUAL SIGNED DOCUMENT — eighth consecutive pass with none, and one lane still reads it as having expired Friday. That conflict is printed rather than hidden, because reinstatement and extension are not the same instrument and the call is today. 🆕 THE CASE FOR REINSTATING GOT THINNER OVER THE WEEKEND, SAID PLAINLY: the unrepresented buyer who phoned Thursday about the workshop and garage STOOD DOWN Sunday afternoon — his wife wants to hold off — and you answered him yourself. He was the single strongest live argument for holding the price. ⭐ THE PRICING PICTURE IS OTHERWISE UNCHANGED: day 92, no price change since May, exactly one written offer all summer, the 8/11 'full-price showing' this board carried for two days never happened by the agent's own admission, and Friday's tour ran and produced total silence. ⭐ Both feedback forms this house has ever produced left every price field blank — the objections were the upstairs bathroom and a compartmentalized interior. Nobody who has walked it has ever named a different number. ⚠️ Quote $450,000 only until the sellers rule.

listings.status: ✅ Under contract $899K — closes THURSDAY, and it is still the quietest high-risk file you have
listings.note: ⏰ THREE DAYS OUT AND THIS IS THE NEAREST HARD DATE ON THE BOARD. ✅ What is verified and good: the appraisal is complete and clean on the lender's own words, the repair addendum is fully executed, the septic inspection ran 8/4, and the closing invite matches the stored state on the engine's own check. ⭐ CLOSING IS THURSDAY 8/20 AT 3:00 PM at the closing attorney's office. ✅ THE BROKERAGE ISSUED THE COMMISSION DOCUMENT SATURDAY — the step three separate reminders had been chasing — which starts the payment clock on the largest number closing this month. ⚠️ THE HONEST WORRY IS THE SILENCE, NOT A PROBLEM: this desk has called it the quietest high-risk file in the book for a week and nothing has come in since. Three days out with no traffic is worth one confirmation call to the attorney today rather than an assumption. ⚠️ AND IT MATTERS MORE THAN USUAL THIS WEEK: the funds from this closing land somewhere between late this month and early next, which is AFTER the tightest cash week of the quarter. This closing does not rescue this week, and planning as though it does is the one real risk on an otherwise clean file. ⛔ The old 8/14 close date is retired — do not re-print it anywhere. ⭐ A closing this size is the strongest referral moment you will get this month, and the review-ask on the last funded closing is still untouched at twenty-eight days.

listings.status: 📸 Coming to market $185K — the photo shoot is THIS MORNING
listings.note: 📸 THE SHOOT IS TODAY AND BOTH HALVES OF IT ARE CLOSED — the photographer is booked and the seller has been told, ruled on your word Sunday at 12:14 after this board spent a weekend calling it the loudest red row on the file. ✅ EVERYTHING ELSE ON THIS FILE ALREADY WENT RIGHT: both sellers executed all seven documents Friday morning, at 11:41 and 11:49, on three separate receipts, and the milestone engine fired this address for the first time in its life. 🔴 WHAT LANDS TODAY BEHIND THE CAMERA IS THE MLS INPUT PREP — that is the step between a photo shoot and a live listing, and it is the only thing standing between this house and the market this weekend. 🔴 AND THE HALF NOBODY HAS EVER WORKED IS STILL OPEN, ON THE DAY IT WAS PROMISED. Remember what she actually came in saying, unprompted: very interested in a property AND about ready to list their own. This is the LIST half of a two-sided deal. The BUY half has never been touched, no criteria or budget is recorded anywhere in the system, and your own words to her were 'want to look Monday?' — which is today. ⭐ WORTH KEEPING AS A PROCESS NOTE: the desk had staged a written note to the seller and then reversed itself once you confirmed you had told her directly. That reversal was printed rather than quietly dropped, which is the only way these boards stay worth reading. ⚠️ The $185,000 price is your own ruling and is quotable, but it still has no primary MLS source behind it.

listings.status: 🔥 Active $295K — top of a buyer's list, and the call is now three days old
listings.note: 🔥 THE BEST NEWS ON THE BOARD IS ALSO THE OLDEST UNWORKED THING ON IT. Amy G. of Ethos International filed Saturday at 11:24 PM off that afternoon's tour: interested — YES, staged 3, and in her own words her buyers have just started looking, really like the property, and have put it at the top of their list. ⭐ SHE IS THE SAME AGENT WHO PHONED YOU FROM INSIDE THE HOUSE mid-showing, so the channel is already warm — this is a returned call, not a cold approach. ✅ THE PRICING QUESTION IS NOW ANSWERED AS FIRMLY AS FEEDBACK CAN ANSWER IT: she left BOTH price fields blank, making FIVE consecutive reads since the 8/5 cut where nobody argued the number. Every read that ever said TOO HIGH was filed while the ask was $299,000. A $4,000 experiment that worked — do not reopen price with this seller. 🔴 THE LIVE ITEM IS THE BASEMENT LIGHTS. She reported on the phone that they would not turn on; you answered the garage half by text and that half is closed. This half is not. ⭐ She scored staging a 3 and is the ONLY agent to score staging since the cut, so she is worth asking what she would change. 🔴 Two co-op agents who expressed buyer interest still do not know the price moved — both chips overdue since 8/8, now nine days. ⛔ Quote $295,000 only. ⛔ Call, don't email. ⚠️ One older thread is still unanswered: the 8/10 agent asked in writing whether the ceiling stains came from a previous leak. 📊 Seventeen showings all-time, still the highest-traffic active in the book — and no new booking since Saturday.

listings.status: 🔥 Active $550K — two showings in one Saturday, and still not one word back
listings.note: 🆕 TWO SEPARATE AGENTS WALKED THIS HOUSE ON SATURDAY, SIX HOURS APART — one at 11:10 in the morning and one at 4:00 in the afternoon, taking the all-time counter from 41 to 42 in a single day. ✅ THE SOURCE PROBLEM THIS BOARD FLAGGED FOR TWO DAYS IS CLOSED: both notices print the list price at $550,000. Every prior notice on file printed $559,000 because they all predated the cut, so the price was one source seen repeatedly. It is now confirmed independently and it is quotable. ⭐ THE TIMING IS THE POINT — the cut went live 8/13 and produced two tours inside forty-eight hours on a house whose last read called it too high. That is the market answering the question directly. 🔴 NEITHER TOUR HAS FILED FEEDBACK AND BOTH ARE NOW PAST TWO FULL DAYS, AND THE 8/10 TOUR BEFORE THEM NEVER DID EITHER — three showings deep with nothing returned, which is the single biggest information gap on the board and it did not move over the weekend. 🔴 THE ITEM THIS BOARD HAS CARRIED UNACTIONED FOR THREE WEEKS IS STILL THE ONE THAT WOULD MOVE THE NEEDLE: the 7/23 read said dirty plus GLITCHING ELECTRICAL, and the 8/4 read scored staging 2 of 5, the lowest this listing has ever recorded, against a 4 three weeks earlier from an agent who called the price JUST RIGHT. The house did not get more expensive between those visits — it got less presentable. An electrician and a cleaner remain cheaper than another lost buyer. ⚠️ THE PRICE-CHANGE CREATIVE CAUGHT ITSELF AGAIN THIS MORNING: the corrected carousel had slipped from draft to scheduled without approval — the SECOND time this month a post has done that — and the marketing lane pulled it back to draft and raised it. The live 8/10 post still carries $559,000 until you approve the replacement.

listings.status: 🎉 Under contract $390,000 — the response WENT OUT, and the draft still in the folder is a duplicate to delete
listings.note: ✅ CORRECTION WORTH READING, BECAUSE THIS BOARD HAD IT WRONG TWICE. The inspection-response letter to the sellers was NOT sitting unsent — you sent it yourself Saturday morning at 9:54. The document still sitting in the drafts folder is a DUPLICATE created six minutes later, and it is flagged for DELETION rather than aging as pending follow-up. Two separate reads called it 'unsent for 24 hours'; both were reading the copy, not the original. ⚠️ It is now roughly two days old and still nothing has deleted it — a hazard, not a task, and the oldest untidy thing in the drafts folder. ⭐ THE SHAPE OF THE ASK IS THE STORY AND IT IS GOOD NEWS: they inspected seventy-one items, flagged sixty-eight at some level, and then asked for exactly three. That is a reasonable buyer. ⭐ THE RECOMMENDATION YOU SENT IS TWO YESES AND A HOLD — agree to the basement leak and to a scoped HVAC service, and on the roof do not say no, say give us a few days and our own licensed roofer's report. The inspector wrote in the same section that he cannot determine the roof's age or remaining life, which is the report itself saying the roof question is unanswered. ⚠️ TWO THINGS BEFORE FIGHTING THE ROOF: this is FHA, so the appraiser can raise it independently, and the concession room left under the FHA cap is small, so this gets solved with work rather than a check. ✅ The sellers have acknowledged the roof-holdback approach. 🔴 THE OPEN QUESTION NOW IS A DEADLINE NOBODY CAN READ: the date the buyers' repair-resolution window actually closes does not exist anywhere in this system, on this file or any other. That gap is the subject of a queued proposal and it is live right here, today. ⭐ Closing 10/23 — roughly ten weeks, which is a luxury most files do not get.

listings.status: ✅ Under contract — both gates cleared, close 8/28, and the seller is STILL waiting on a call
listings.note: ✅ STILL THE CLEANEST FILE ON YOUR BOARD ON PAPER. Both gates are behind you: the inspection ran 8/5 at noon and the appraisal 8/7 at 9:00 AM, both on primary notices, and the 8/28 close date was cross-checked against three sources again and passed. ⭐ AN INSPECTION AND AN APPRAISAL BOTH SPENT IS THE STRONGEST POSITION ANY DEAL ON THIS BOARD OCCUPIES. ✅ AND THE ONE THING THAT COULD HAVE BITTEN IT GOT CAUGHT WITHOUT YOU: your operations manager chased and closed the payoff item on 8/14, with two status comments on the record. That is the catch that protects the close, and it is worth acknowledging to her — especially this week. 🔴 AND YET THE SELLER HAS BEEN WAITING ON A RETURNED CALL SINCE LAST TUESDAY — six days now, mid-transaction, on the deal with the least to worry about. ⭐ A CLIENT MID-TRANSACTION WHO CALLS AND GETS NOTHING BACK IS THE MOST EXPENSIVE SILENCE YOU CAN BUY, because it costs the referral rather than the closing. Today is Client Day and this is exactly the row it exists for. ⚠️ The appraised value still has not come back — day eleven, reported as a single-source observation rather than an alarm, and worth one call to the lender on the same pass. ⚠️ One number remains unruled and it is worth real money on an otherwise settled deal: the buyer's agent asked for a specific co-op commission and nobody has ever answered.

listings.status: 🎉 Under contract $162K — inspection held, both price reads validated the number
listings.note: ✅ THE FIRST GATE IS BEHIND YOU — inspection confirmed and held 8/13 at 10:00 AM; MLS reads CONTINGENT. ✅ THE PAPERWORK ITEM IS CLOSED, NOT PENDING: the contract went out with all signatures, the contract-to-close packet reached title 8/12, and the closing attorney confirmed receipt. 🔴 ONE THREAD IS NOT CLOSED AND IT GOT LOUDER THIS MORNING: the seller's initials on a specific paragraph have been sitting unsent for five days on your operations manager's side, and this morning's inbox triage raised it as closing-critical rather than housekeeping. On a file this clean that is a process gap — but it is the kind that becomes a deal risk quietly. ⭐ TWO INDEPENDENT READS NOW VALIDATE THIS PRICE — the agent who wrote the offer called it JUST RIGHT, and a late form off the 8/7 tour said interested No but PRICED JUST RIGHT with a staging 3 of 5. That is the kind of evidence that matters if anything wobbles before 9/14. ⭐ THE BACKSTORY IS WORTH KEEPING ON THE RECORD: the buyer's agent said her client really liked it but needed to save more for a down payment, and this desk argued for two weeks against reading that as a price signal — she had written JUST RIGHT on the same form. She wrote. Offer to acceptance in twenty-eight minutes. Patience was the right call. ⭐ Closing 9/14.

listings.status: 🔥 Active $184K — a 'VERY interested' buyer is now nine days unworked
listings.note: 🔥 THE LISTING THIS BOARD ONCE CALLED INVISIBLE PRODUCED THREE TOURS IN A SINGLE SATURDAY, all three forms filed within ninety minutes of each other on 8/8. One answered the interest question with the single word 'Very' and left every other field blank — which is exactly why it needs a phone call: the enthusiasm is on record and the reason is not. ✅ THE $5,000 CUT IS VERIFIED LIVE AND PUBLIC — the MLS line on all three notices reads $184,000, so the old do-not-quote hedge is retired. 🔴 THE REAL FINDING IS THE OBJECTION AND IT IS VERIFIED THREE WAYS: the problem is SIZE, not price. The clearest read says it in four words — 'Just too small.' ⛔ NO DISCOUNT REACHES A SIZE OBJECTION. The answer here is AUDIENCE — first-time buyers, downsizers, investors — and a price conversation with this seller would be solving the wrong problem. This board argued for a cut here for weeks on the strength of silence; the showings arrived and said something different, and that earlier read is withdrawn. 🔴 That Saturday burst has now fully decayed with the one phone call still unmade, and no new booking has come in since.

listings.status: 🔥 Active $599K package — two more names off the ad this weekend, and the septic answer is STILL undelivered
listings.note: 🔥 THE AD PRODUCED TWICE MORE OVER THE WEEKEND — a buyer came off the 19-lot listing Sunday afternoon and registered on your IDX site four minutes later, and a brand-new name arrived at 7:00 this morning and was answered inside six minutes. That is eight names off this one ad while every other ad in the portfolio has produced zero. ✅ THE DELIVERABLE WAS LOCATED FRIDAY — the 19-lot plat, precisely what the open buyer chip had been waiting on since he answered 'Yes', and it went out the same morning. 🔴 THE THING THAT SHOULD BOTHER YOU MOST ON THIS FILE IS NOT THE COUNTY, IT IS THE HANDOFF, AND IT IS NOW DAY FIVE: the builder asked the septic perc question on 8/12, your operations manager researched and answered it completely, and that answer has been sitting on her board since Friday with nobody reading it back to him. The work was done; the delivery never happened. ⭐ THE PERC QUESTION ITSELF IS PRICED RATHER THAN BLOCKED: the county takes record searches in person only, weekdays 8:00 to 3:30, at a per-record fee — across nineteen lots that is a four-figure errand. ⭐ SO THE CHOICE IS THREE-WAY, NOT TWO: send someone for all nineteen, narrow the pull to the lots a buyer is actually asking about, or try the free path first and ask the developer, who almost certainly already holds the perc results from platting. ⭐ PERC DECIDES BUILDABILITY AND BUILDABILITY DECIDES PRICE PER LOT, which is why this one question governs the whole package. ⚠️ Two builder outreach addresses hard-bounced permanently after 48 hours of retries — part of the builder audience received nothing at all, and those two need replacing rather than resending.

listings.status: 🔴 Buyer-side $2.35M — the counter has never been put on paper, day 27
listings.note: 🔴 THE LARGEST SINGLE NUMBER ON YOUR BOARD, ROUGHLY $36K OF GCI, AND THE WHOLE COST OF MOVING IT IS TWENTY MINUTES OF WRITING. The listing side has asked repeatedly since 7/21 to be moved forward and has never received a written position from your side. ⚠️ STATED HONESTLY: a phone call leaves no receipt, so this is ABSENCE rather than proven failure — but what was promised was paper, and there is none on any lane this desk can read. ⭐ WHY IT KEEPS RETURNING: a seller who reverse-offers a buyer is a seller who wants a deal, and the honest answer IS the counter. Sending it is not a favour to them; it is your position on the record. ⚠️ NOT ASSERTED, AND THIS MATTERS BEFORE ANYTHING GOES OVER: the appraisal figure your buyer cited as far under ask is single-sourced from him. Whose appraisal it is, when it was done, and whether it is a formal appraisal at all are all unknown. Do not quote it to the other side as an appraised value. 🛑 A RELATED ITEM IS LIVE, UNRULED, AND NOW CARRIES A SELF-INFLICTED PROBLEM: the counter structure the other side asked for on a separate buyer file — written counter or a subject-to / seller-finance shape — has been waiting on your call since 8/13, and this fleet has now written TWO drafts onto that same thread, the second at 5:55 this morning. Pick one and kill the other; the machine flagged its own duplicate.

listings.status: 🔴 Active — the tenant answer is twenty-four days owed
listings.note: 🔴 THE LONGEST-RUNNING BROKEN PROMISE ON THE BOARD, AND IT CROSSED THREE WEEKS THIS WEEKEND. She left a twenty-two-second voicemail on 7/25 rather than sending a seventh text — which is what a patient client does when nothing comes back — and then escalated THREE TIMES IN TWENTY-SEVEN MINUTES on a Wednesday night: two voicemails and a text. ✅ THE EMERGENCY HALF RESOLVED WITHOUT YOU — power is back on at the property and the tenant paid his balance, both confirmed. ⭐ THE OWED THING IS STILL YOURS: she asked whether the tenant on this unit is out, because he owes another month's rent if he isn't. ⚠️ YOU DO NOT NEED AN ANSWER TO MAKE THIS CALL. 'Still no word from him, here's exactly what I'm doing about it' beats a twenty-fifth day of silence. ⭐ She is not a loose end — she closed with you in June, still opens your market reports, and has an unclosed valuation loop on this same address.

listings.status: 🔴 Active — seventeen days quiet, and the good news is STILL undelivered
listings.note: 🔴 TWO TOURS IN FIVE DAYS AT THE END OF JULY, THEN NOTHING SINCE. On a listing that had gone 126 days with essentially no traffic, that brief burst was the only real activity this file has produced and it has fully decayed. ⭐ THE GOOD NEWS IS STILL UNDELIVERED AT SEVENTEEN DAYS, WHICH MAKES IT THE OLDEST OWED ITEM ON THE BOARD: the 7/31 read came back interested No, but with the price called JUST RIGHT, a 4 of 5 rating, and the comment that the buyers prefer the east end of the beach although they liked this complex. That is a GEOGRAPHY loss, not a price loss, and it is the only independent validation of this list price the file has ever carried. ⚠️ AND IT HAS NOW SLID OUT OF THE FOURTEEN-DAY WINDOW — that read no longer appears in the rolling feedback count on the showing board. The finding is not gone, but the clock on delivering it has run out of runway. ⭐ He is out of state and lives on these reads — lead with the price answer, not the no. ⚠️ A price discrepancy opened during the dark window and is still unresolved: two sources five thousand apart, and neither is quotable until the MLS is read directly.

listings.status: ⚠️ Active $1.15M — biggest listing in the book, seller identity STILL unverified
